chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, who said:

I sent a message to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) that a brother of mine had bought doves from Al-Medina, so we went with them to Makkah. So we performed Umrah and we stayed until the Hajj. Then we brought out the doves along with us, from Makkah to Al-Kufa. So is there anything upon us with regards to that? He (peace be upon him) said to the messenger: 'I think they were delightful (for food). He should slaughter a sheep in place of each bird.'
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for bringing doves into Makkah for food?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the application of *kaffarah* (expiation) for bringing game into the sacred precincts of Mecca, specifically addressing the status of domesticated birds like doves. Imam Al-Hasan (AS) clarifies that if the birds were acquired for culinary delight (*furhah*), the penalty is equivalent to slaughtering a sheep for each bird, reflecting the principle of proportional restitution in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the sanctity of the Haram boundaries and the specific obligations for pilgrims who transport hunted animals across these limits.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub who said,

‘I sent a message to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> that a brother of mine had bought doves from Al-Medina, so we went with it to Makkah. So we performed Umra and we stayed up to the Hajj. Then we brought out the doves along with us, from Makkah to Al-Kufa. So is there anything upon us with regards to that?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said to the messenger: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> thing they were delightful. They should slaughter a sheep in place of each bird’.
en.sarwar: 16. Ahmad ibn Muhammad from has narrated from ibn Faddal from Yunus ibn Ya’qub who has said the following:

“I once sent a message to abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that my brother had purchased pigeons from al-Madinah and we went to Makkah for ‘Umrah. We stayed for Hajj, then we took the pigeon with us from Makkah to al-Kufah; if we owe anything. He (the Imam) said to the messenger, ‘I think they were beautiful.’ He (the Imam) said to him, ‘For every one of them one sheep must be slaughtered.’”
